paragraphs: In the morning, lead small-group cognitive and language training and record behavioral data. At midday, align inclusion arrangements with general education teachers. In the afternoon, provide one-on-one interventions and organize records. Before dismissal, discuss the day's progress with parents and revise the next day's plan.

AI will not replace kindergarten special education teachers, but it will assist with administrative tasks. Tools accelerate assessment scales, progress records, and behavioral analysis, shifting teachers from filling out forms toward understanding children, developing individualized plans, and providing relationship-based interventions. People who only handle administration face displacement, while those skilled in intervention and family-school collaboration become more valuable.
